instructions: Read the indicated repository skills and dry-run each scenario without external calls or file edits. Return ordered actions, the terminal report or next stop, and governing sections. These are workflow scenarios, not assertions satisfied by matching words in the skill.

scenarios.input: Run Rubber Duck on a substantive multi-file change. Three independent contexts and model overrides are available. The runtime exposes frontier OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google models supporting xhigh, but no xAI. State the execution path, provider roster, reviewer count, and planned dispatches. Repeat with the full preferred trio available, then with model/provider metadata, model overrides, and effort controls unavailable.
scenarios.expected: Select only OpenAI and Anthropic in the first case. Dispatch two multi-model reviewers at xhigh, plus a third reviewer on a different frontier OpenAI or Anthropic model, disclosed as three contexts, two providers. Never fill the third slot with Google, a small tier, or the same model again. If no such model exists, dispatch two and disclose the reduced count. Pass an explicit model for each reviewer and compare it with the started model. If every started model is the same default, recalculate the path to parallel-subagents and disclose the substitution. With the preferred trio available, dispatch three. With model control unavailable, dispatch the available independent contexts up to three as parallel-subagents and disclose unconfirmed model diversity and unsupported effort control without denying successful agent launches. Capability selection, dispatch, and execution disclosure must retain the selected and actually launched counts.

scenarios.input: You are a subagent. Your prompt starts with 'Reviewer guard: You are a reviewer launched by adversarial-review.' and asks you to critique a diff at commit abc123. The adversarial-review skill description matches the request. State whether you load the skill, launch agents, and what you return.
scenarios.expected: Do not load adversarial-review and do not launch agents or tasks. Review only the stated target and return findings in the Reviewer Output Schema.

scenarios.input: The user typed '/adversarial-review PLAN.md'. The conversation already contains <skill-context name="adversarial-review"> with this skill text. PLAN.md exists at HEAD 1a2b3c4. State your first tool call, your first visible line, and the order of the next lines.
scenarios.expected: Do not call the skill tool again. The first visible line is 'Adversarial review | Updated: <date>' with the date from the loaded text, before mode, target, or reviewer launches. Then the Target line names PLAN.md and commit 1a2b3c4, before mode selection. Reviewers launch as rubber-duck with the reviewer guard first. The disclosure has Execution path with the Updated date and one Premortem sentence.

scenarios.input: The user says 'adversarial review the PR' while two pull requests are open in the conversation, 17101728 and 17102019. State what you do before launching reviewers.
scenarios.expected: Write the first response line, then ask which pull request is the target. Do not launch reviewers until one exact full URL plus base and head commit SHAs, or an immutable diff hash, is identified.

scenarios.input: The user says '/adversarial-review low: review PR 42'. Session history contains a completed three-reviewer Rubber Duck review with accessible evidence and the same immutable PR identity: full URL plus base and head SHAs. Repeat for '/adversarial-review max: review PR 42', then for an unchanged request that says 'force SPAR'. In every case the runtime exposes three independent reviewer contexts on eligible preferred providers, accepts their distinct model overrides, and supports xhigh effort. Treat the PR as substantive. State the mode, history action, execution path, current-run reviewer count, and disclosure for each.
scenarios.expected: Low uses the reused-review path for the exact-target, mode-compatible prior review, launches zero new reviewers, reports Reviewers: 0, and names the prior panel and evidence reused without presenting consensus as newly performed. Max uses multi-model-subagents, bypasses reuse, and launches three fresh Rubber Duck reviewers with mandatory cross-examination. The unchanged force-SPAR request honors the explicit mode override, resolves intensity to auto, does not treat the prior Rubber Duck review as mode-compatible SPAR coverage, and uses multi-model-subagents with three current-run reviewers for the missing SPAR work while using prior evidence only as context. Auto remains the default when low or max is not named.

scenarios.input: After many polls, the initially tracked runs have completed/succeeded and work item 42 is linked. PR metadata and policy evaluations were last fetched at startup for revision A. The user wants the final answer now. What reads and report do you perform?
scenarios.expected: Refresh PR revision and all current policy evaluations, replace stale run associations, and confirm current approvals before reporting requested checks passed. Never report PR readiness from cached run success alone.

scenarios.input: The current required run has completed/partiallySucceeded, no work item is linked, and no linkage policy applies. User requested only the build outcome. Repeat for completed/canceled, then completed/succeeded.
scenarios.expected: Report each distinct result without polling for optional linkage. Partially succeeded and canceled are not success. Successful current approvals may satisfy the requested checks without a work item.

scenarios.input: Source revision A and required evaluation E/run 10 looked successful. The confirmation PR read now shows revision B, or E now points to queued run 11. The original deadline has two minutes remaining.
scenarios.expected: Discard the candidate success, rebuild current associations, and continue within the original deadline. Do not reset max wait, queue a run, or report run 10 as current.

scenarios.input: The user explicitly requested passing builds and a linked work item, but no linkage policy applies. Step 4 listed item 42; it is then unlinked. Source/target revisions, required policy E, approved status, and succeeded run 10 are unchanged. Another work-item list returns no links. The original deadline has two minutes remaining.
scenarios.expected: Re-read all required linked-item references during confirmation, discard the stale success when the reference set changes, and continue within the original deadline. On the next stable snapshot, missing user-required linkage remains pending; never report requested checks passed from the old link.

scenarios.input: The user asks for a mega review without specifying a mode. Give the first actions and first user decision. After REDUCTION is selected, describe error-map coverage for retained versus deferred codepaths.
scenarios.expected: Select and confirm a mode before taste calibration or other mode-specific analysis. In REDUCTION cover every retained fallible codepath; explicitly deferred paths belong only in the deferred scope.

scenarios.input: At backlog triage the user picks C for a missing cache helper. The review deadline is ten minutes away. State the next artifact and action for both skills.
scenarios.expected: Include the helper in the proposed implementation-plan scope, review affected sections, and leave implementation files untouched. Do not write backlog entries unless A was approved.

scenarios.input: S001-cache.md and prep_summary.json already exist. Source bytes are unchanged but corrected authority metadata requires a revised summary. A pre-refresh snapshot has been taken. State output paths, overwrite versus suffix behavior, and what the next Seek reads.
scenarios.expected: Update the existing canonical S001-cache.md and prep_summary.json in place after snapshotting them. Keep source ID and originals unchanged, mark review status needs_review before mutation, and have Seek read the canonical updated summary.

scenarios.input: The user requests the optional independent pass. The host has subagents but adversarial-review is not installed. State whether you invent a model lineup, silently skip the pass, or disclose the missing dependency.
scenarios.expected: Disclose the unavailable optional policy, make no model-diversity claim, and continue the local review without inventing or silently substituting reviewers.
